name: Baobab Fare
tagline: East African cooking from a Burundian couple on Woodward, with a small market inside.
description: Baobab Fare serves East African food and runs a small market, and it means to be a meeting place for immigrants and other Detroiters. It is run by Hamissi Mamba and Nadia Nijimbere, a married couple who came to Detroit from Burundi. They ran pop-ups in 2016 and 2017 and won the Hatch Detroit contest before opening.

_verified.note: Black-owned: owners named by CityBird (Feb 2025), Visit Detroit couples list and StarChefs. Open: own site live with current address, phone and online ordering.

name: Flood's Bar & Grille
tagline: Downtown bar and grill near Greektown, on St. Antoine since 1987.
description: Flood's is a downtown bar and grill near Greektown. It has been on St. Antoine since 1987 and is listed in Black Bottom Archives' Black business directory.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Black Bottom Archives directory and A Healthier Michigan list (Feb 2025). Open: own site lists an Oct 15, 2026 event. 'Since 1987' from own site.

name: Yum Village
tagline: Afro-Caribbean meals in New Center from chef Godwin Ihentuge.
description: Yum Village serves ready-to-eat Afro-Caribbean meals and offers delivery from its spot on Woodward in New Center. Chef Godwin Ihentuge runs it.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Godwin Ihentuge named by CityBird (Feb 2025) and Metro Times. Open: own site live with menu and ordering. Phone left null (not confirmed). CityBird printed the address as 64500 Woodward, a typo; own site address used.

name: Ivy Kitchen + Cocktails
tagline: Chef-driven dinner and cocktails on East Jefferson from owner Nya Marshall.
description: Ivy Kitchen + Cocktails is a sit-down restaurant and cocktail bar on the east side. Owner Nya Marshall opened it on a long-empty block of East Jefferson, and it rolled out new fall dishes in late 2024.

_verified.note: Black-owned: owner Nya Marshall named by Metro Times; on A Healthier Michigan list (Feb 2025). Open: WDIV Live in the D story dated Nov 1, 2024 on new fall dishes. Website domain did not resolve, so website, phone and zip left null.

name: Shell Shock'd Tacos
tagline: Late-night fusion tacos and crunch wraps in the Cass Corridor.
description: Shell Shock'd Tacos serves fusion tacos, burritos and crunch wraps, open until 2 a.m. on weekends. Margo Moon and chef Cedric Andrews started it as a pop-up in 2021 and opened the Willis Street storefront in 2023. Its taco de pollo won Detroit's Taco Showdown at Eastern Market in July 2025.

_verified.note: Black-owned: owners named by CityBird (Feb 2025) and Visit Detroit new Black-owned restaurants list. Open: Metro Times Taco Showdown coverage (2025 win) and 2025 Visit Detroit listing. No own website or phone confirmed. Founded year is the 2021 pop-up start per BridgeDetroit.

name: Ima
tagline: Noodles, ramen and rice bowls from chef Mike Ransom, with an izakaya in Corktown.
description: Ima serves noodles, ramen and rice bowls. Chef Mike Ransom runs the Corktown izakaya flagship plus a Cass Avenue shop and a Madison Heights location.

_verified.note: Black-owned: owner Mike Ransom named by CityBird (Feb 2025) and A Healthier Michigan (Feb 2025). Open: own site live, footer 2026, lists three locations. AHM gave 2015 Michigan Ave; own site's 2100 Michigan Ave used. Phone not confirmed.

name: SuperCrisp
tagline: Hot dogs and burgers with Asian-inspired twists from the Ima team.
description: SuperCrisp is a Midtown counter spot serving hot dogs and burgers with Asian-inspired twists, including a curry burger on a halal beef patty. It is run by chef Mike Ransom, who also runs Ima.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Mike Ransom named by CityBird and A Healthier Michigan (both Feb 2025). Open: own site live; listed in Visit Detroit's 2025 new Black-owned restaurants. Note supercrispdetroit.com is a parked domain; supercrisp.com is the real site.

name: Savoy
tagline: Steak and seafood with a jazz-inspired feel in East English Village.
description: Savoy is a steak and seafood restaurant on East Warren with a jazz-inspired feel. It closed for renovations from late June to mid August 2026.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Visit Detroit new Black-owned restaurants list (2025). Open: own site footer 2026, photos dated March 2026, and a notice of renovation closure June 27 to Aug 13, 2026. Owners not named in sources.

name: SavannahBlue
tagline: Downtown dining room on Times Square.
description: SavannahBlue is a sit-down restaurant downtown on Times Square. It is on A Healthier Michigan's 2025 list of Black-owned Detroit restaurants.

_verified.note: Black-owned: A Healthier Michigan list (Feb 2025). Open: own site live. Owners and cuisine details not confirmed in the sources opened, so copy is kept short and verdict is confirmed rather than open.

name: Fixins Soul Kitchen Detroit
tagline: Southern comfort food in Paradise Valley from former NFL player Kevin Johnson.
description: Fixins serves Southern plates like fried chicken, catfish and mac and cheese in Paradise Valley. Founder Kevin Johnson, a former NFL player, built the menu from his family's recipes, and this is the chain's fourth location.

_verified.note: Black-owned: founder Kevin Johnson named by Visit Detroit (2025). Open: own site with Detroit menus dated Jan 3, 2026. Slug has -detroit because fixins-soul-kitchen is taken by another city.

name: Parlay Detroit
tagline: Sports bar near the stadiums with brick oven pizza and gold-flake mac and cheese.
description: Parlay is a downtown sports bar a short walk from the stadiums, with big screens, cocktails and a happy hour. The kitchen is known for brick oven pizza and its 24 Karat Gold Mac and Cheese.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Visit Detroit new Black-owned restaurants list (2025). Open: own site blog posts July to October 2026. Owners not named in sources.

name: Joe Louis Southern Kitchen
tagline: Southern brunch in New Center named for the Brown Bomber.
description: Joe Louis Southern Kitchen is a brunch spot in New Center named after the boxer Joe Louis. The menu includes cinnamon roll flapjacks, cobbler French toast and The Brown Bomber biscuits.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Visit Detroit new Black-owned restaurants (2025) and A Healthier Michigan (Feb 2025). Open: own site live with hours. AHM listed 3100 W Grand Blvd; own site and Visit Detroit give 6549 Woodward, used here. Owners not named.

name: Louisiana Creole Gumbo
tagline: Creole gumbo near Eastern Market, with more locations around metro Detroit.
description: Louisiana Creole Gumbo serves Creole food, led by the gumbo in its name, from a shop on Gratiot near Eastern Market. A Healthier Michigan lists other locations on West Seven Mile and in Farmington Hills.

_verified.note: Black-owned: A Healthier Michigan list (Feb 2025). Open: own site live with hours. AHM listed 2051 Gratiot; own site's 2830 Gratiot used. Owners not named in sources.

name: Good Cakes and Bakes
tagline: Scratch-made cakes and pastries on Livernois from April and Michelle Anderson.
description: Good Cakes and Bakes is a bakery on the Avenue of Fashion making cakes, cupcakes and cookies from scratch with local produce when they can. It is owned by April and Michelle Anderson, and Visit Detroit calls it a nationally celebrated Black LGBTQ-owned business.

_verified.note: Black-owned: owners named by Visit Detroit couples list. Open: own site with hours and online ordering; Light Up Livernois 2025 festival participant.

name: Empire Kitchen & Cocktails
tagline: Brush Park restaurant and cocktail bar on Woodward.
description: Empire Kitchen & Cocktails is a restaurant and bar in Brush Park serving dinner, brunch and cocktails. It is on A Healthier Michigan's 2025 list of Black-owned Detroit restaurants.

_verified.note: Black-owned: A Healthier Michigan list (Feb 2025). Open: own site live with hours. Owners not named in the sources opened.

name: The Kitchen by Cooking with Que
tagline: Plant-based cafe, cocktails and event space in New Center from chef Que Broden.
description: The Kitchen is a plant-based cafe and event space where, in its own words, vegans and meat-eaters coexist. It offers craft cocktails, meal prep, catering and private events. Founder Quiana "Que" Broden also sells a frozen vegan mac and cheese online.

_verified.note: Black-owned: founder Quiana Broden named by CityBird (Feb 2025); also on A Healthier Michigan list. Open: own site restaurant page live with 2025 shipping notice and 2026 footer; GVSU 2025 story. Address from CityBird and AHM, not the own site. Phone and hours not listed.

name: LYV Detroit
tagline: Restaurant and lounge on the Avenue of Fashion with Soul Food Sundays.
description: LYV is a restaurant and lounge on Livernois open Wednesday through Sunday, with late hours on weekends. Sundays are Soul Food Sunday, and the room is available for private events early in the week.

_verified.note: Black-owned: A Healthier Michigan list (Feb 2025), directory-style proof only. Open: own site live with current weekly hours (footer 2024, no dated posts). Owners not named.

name: The Jamaican Pot
tagline: Jamaican kitchen at Eight Mile and Hubbell, plus a mobile kitchen.
description: The Jamaican Pot cooks Jamaican food from its kitchen at Eight Mile and Hubbell. It also runs a mobile kitchen and a counter inside a party store in St. Clair Shores with Taco Tuesday and Jamaican Food Friday.

_verified.note: Black-owned: A Healthier Michigan list (Feb 2025), directory-style proof only. Open: own site with current hours for both locations, footer 2014 to 2026. Owners not named. Top-up 2026-10-15: wrote Eight Mile Rd W as W 8 Mile Rd so the address geocodes.

name: Sweet Potato Sensations
tagline: Sweet potato bakery on Lahser on the west side.
description: Sweet Potato Sensations is a west side bakery built around the sweet potato. It is on A Healthier Michigan's 2025 list of Black-owned Detroit restaurants.

_verified.note: Black-owned: A Healthier Michigan list (Feb 2025). Activity thin: own site live but shows no dated posts or hours, so kept as draft. Founding year and owners seen only in a search snippet, left null.

name: Baker's Keyboard Lounge
tagline: Jazz club on Livernois with a piano-shaped bar, billed as the world's oldest.
description: Baker's Keyboard Lounge is a jazz club on Livernois that has long claimed to be the world's oldest, and it is known for its piano-shaped bar. It has been owned since 2011 by Eric Whitaker and Hugh "Bill" Smith.

_verified.note: Black-owned: owners Eric Whitaker and Hugh Bill Smith per WDET (Oct 2024) and Metro Times coverage; on A Healthier Michigan list. Open: Live in the D story June 17, 2026. bakerskeyboardlounge.com did not resolve, so website and phone left null.

name: Bert's Marketplace
tagline: Eastern Market jazz room and food court with Black Detroit history on the walls.
description: Bert's is an Eastern Market spot with a jazz room, a food court and a theater, with live jazz and blues and karaoke on Saturdays. Murals by Curtis Lewis and items from Bert Dearing Jr.'s own collection cover Black Detroit history. Dearing has run it since 1987.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Bert Dearing Jr. named by Model D (revisited profile, April 2, 2018); on A Healthier Michigan list (Feb 2025). Open: WXYZ NFL Draft night market coverage (2024) and AHM 2025 listing. Own site refused connection, so website null. Details may have changed since the 2018 profile.

name: Charles H. Wright Museum of African American History
tagline: Midtown museum of African American history, founded in 1965.
description: The Wright Museum holds exhibits on African American history and culture. Dr. Charles H. Wright founded it in 1965, and it marked its 60th anniversary in 2025.

_verified.note: Black-led institution founded by Dr. Charles H. Wright (nonprofit, not a private owner). Open: 60th anniversary programming in 2025 per own site and Detroit PBS; site live with current hours and tickets.

name: The Heidelberg Project
tagline: Tyree Guyton's outdoor art environment on Heidelberg Street, 40 years running.
description: The Heidelberg Project is an outdoor art environment across the 3600 block of Heidelberg Street on the east side. Artist Tyree Guyton started it in 1986, and in 2026 he was named the Kresge Eminent Artist.

_verified.note: Black-founded nonprofit art environment by Tyree Guyton. Open: Kresge 2026 Eminent Artist announcement and WDET Feb 2, 2026 interview on 40 years. Address is the 3600 block of Heidelberg per own site.

name: N'Namdi Center for Contemporary Art
tagline: Contemporary art center in Midtown founded by gallerist George N'Namdi.
description: The N'Namdi Center shows contemporary art in Midtown's art district. It was founded by George N'Namdi, a longtime Detroit gallerist.

_verified.note: Black-owned: founder George N'Namdi named by CityBird (Feb 2025). Open: own site shows a 2026 exhibition invitation. Instagram not confirmed.

name: Sherwood Forest Art Gallery
tagline: Family-owned gallery of art from the African diaspora on the Avenue of Fashion.
description: Sherwood Forest Art Gallery is a family-owned gallery and shop on Livernois with paintings, masks, sculptures and prints from the African diaspora. It is run by Toney Hughes Sr. and Toney Hughes Jr.

_verified.note: Black-owned: owners named by Model D; listed in Metro Times Black-owned galleries. Open: Light Up Livernois 2025 festival participant. No website or phone confirmed.

name: Centric Place
tagline: Farmington Hills coworking and event space built around Black arts and business.
description: Centric Place is a coworking and event space that calls itself a hub for Black arts, culture and entrepreneurship. It rents meeting rooms and event halls and houses the Blackbird Gallery. It is owned by Racheal and Gerrard Allen.

_verified.note: Black-owned: owners named by Visit Detroit couples list. Open: own site live with current room pricing, footer 2025. No dated events seen. Suburb of Detroit.

name: Source Booksellers
tagline: Independent bookstore on Cass Avenue in Midtown, run by Janet Webster Jones.
description: Source Booksellers is an independent bookstore on Cass Avenue in Midtown. Janet Webster Jones runs it, and she has been selling books since 1989.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Janet Webster Jones named by CityBird (Feb 2025) and Visit Detroit bookstores list. Open: own site taking 2026 preorders.

name: God's World Superstore
tagline: West side Christian bookstore tied to gospel music, open since 1979.
description: God's World is a Christian bookstore on West Seven Mile that serves churchgoers, recording artists and authors, and it is closely tied to gospel music. Larry Robinson founded it in 1979, and it is one of Detroit's oldest bookstores.

_verified.note: Black-owned: founder Larry Robinson named by Visit Detroit bookstores list; article does not confirm current ownership. Open: own site live with Mon to Sat hours, footer to 2025.

name: Mature
tagline: Men's lifestyle clothier in the Fisher Building from Darryl and DeKoven Humes.
description: Mature is a men's lifestyle clothier in the historic Fisher Building. It is run by Darryl and DeKoven Humes.

_verified.note: Black-owned: owners named by CityBird (Feb 2025) and Live in the D. Open: Live in the D story June 14, 2024 and Crain's Fisher Building retail story. Website, phone and founded year not confirmed.

name: Bleu Bowtique
tagline: Men's neckwear and accessories on Cass Avenue.
description: Bleu Bowtique sells men's neckwear and accessories from a shop on Cass Avenue. It is owned by Ne'Gyle Beaman.

_verified.note: Black-owned: owner Ne'Gyle Beaman named by CityBird (Feb 2025). Open: own site live with store hours.

name: The Lip Bar
tagline: Melissa Butler's beauty brand, with its flagship store downtown.
description: The Lip Bar's downtown flagship sells the brand's lipsticks and makeup and offers glam services, a brow bar and private events. Founder Melissa Butler started the brand, and its site says it is founded and owned by women of color.

_verified.note: Black-owned: founder Melissa Butler (Wikipedia, citing Black Enterprise and EBONY); own site says founded and owned by women of color. Open: flagship page with current hours and 2026 footer. Founded year left null.

name: Textures by Nefertiti
tagline: Natural hair salon and spa in New Center from Nefertiti Harris.
description: Textures by Nefertiti is a hair salon and spa on Woodward in New Center. Owner Nefertiti Harris opened the space as a Motor City Match winner.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Black Bottom Archives directory, DEGC grand opening post, CityBird (Feb 2025). Activity thin: own site and booking link live but no dated 2024 to 2026 content seen, so kept as draft.

name: Pillar + Pride
tagline: Vitamins and supplements from Randi and Tyree Williams, sold online.
description: Pillar + Pride sells vitamins and supplements online. It is run by Randi and Tyree Williams, who also run community programs in Detroit.

_verified.note: Black-owned: owners named by Visit Detroit couples list. Open: own site footer 2026; it says the shop is no longer open for walk-in and products are available online only, so listed as virtual and the old W Seven Mile address was not used.

name: Detroit People's Food Co-op
tagline: Black-led, community-owned grocery co-op in the North End.
description: The Detroit People's Food Co-op is a full-service grocery store owned by its members, with produce, prepared meals, and classes on nutrition and cooking. It is Black-led, and Malik Yakini is its founder.

_verified.note: Black-led and community-owned per Visit Detroit grocery list (founder Malik Yakini) and own site. Open: own site live with current hours.

name: Linwood Fresh Market
tagline: Neighborhood market on Linwood with produce, juices and meal kits.
description: Linwood Fresh Market sells fresh produce from Eastern Market and local growers, made-to-order smoothies and juices, deli items and meal kits. Founder Sonya Greene opened it as part of a block redevelopment called The Shift.

_verified.note: Black-owned: founder Sonya Greene named by Visit Detroit Black-owned grocery list. Open: own site with Mon to Sat hours, footer 2026.

name: Liberty Bank and Trust
tagline: Black-owned bank with a branch on Woodward in the North End.
description: Liberty Bank and Trust was chartered in New Orleans in 1972 and calls itself one of the largest Black-owned banks in the country. It came to Detroit when it acquired Home Federal Savings, and it runs a branch on Woodward Avenue.

_verified.note: Black-owned: own site calls it one of the largest Black-owned banks. Open: own branch page lists the Detroit Woodward branch. FDIC MDI list not opened. Slug has -detroit since other cities use this bank.

name: D-Town Farm
tagline: Seven-acre Rouge Park farm run by the Detroit Black Community Food Sovereignty Network.
description: D-Town Farm is a seven-acre farm in Rouge Park run by the Detroit Black Community Food Sovereignty Network. The network marks its 20th anniversary in 2026.

_verified.note: Black-led farm per DBCFSN own site and Black Farmers Index. Open: Michigan Chronicle/Telegram story Jan 9, 2025 and network site live in 2026. dtownfarm.com did not resolve, so the network site and Instagram are used.

name: Oakland Avenue Urban Farm
tagline: North End urban farm with a seasonal Saturday market, growing since 2000.
description: Oakland Avenue Urban Farm grows fruits and vegetables on lots in the North End and runs a Saturday farm market. Rev. Bertha L. Carter founded it in 2000, and Jerry Ann Hebron is executive director.

_verified.note: Black-led farm per Black Farmers Index and WDET. Open: WDET story Sep 8, 2025 on the farm turning 25; own site live.

name: Sanctuary Farms
tagline: East side urban farm now focused on compost, sold by the bag or delivered in bulk.
description: Sanctuary Farms is an east side urban farm that now focuses on making compost, sold in bags or delivered in bulk to Detroit gardeners. It publishes yearly reports on its work.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Black Farmers Index only (directory). Open: own site shows a 2025 annual report and 2026 footer. Zip and phone not confirmed.

name: Deeply Rooted Produce
tagline: Mobile produce market and CSA bringing fresh food to Detroit neighborhoods.
description: Deeply Rooted Produce runs a mobile grocery and CSA that brings fresh produce to Detroit neighborhoods and accepts WIC. It was founded by Dazmonique Carr.

_verified.note: Black-owned: Black Farmers Index (directory). Activity thin: own site live with a 2025 footer but no dated posts, so kept as draft. No street address published.

name: Art Loft
tagline: Cass Avenue boutique for art, decor, clothing and gifts.
description: Art Loft is a boutique on Cass Avenue selling art, home decor, clothing, accessories and gifts. It is owned by Rachael Adadevoh-Woods, who is from Ghana.

_verified.note: Black-owned: owner Rachael Adadevoh-Woods named by CityBird (Feb 2025). Open: own site live, footer 2026. Phone not confirmed.
